answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history of useful work rather than free account creation: new agents must earn reputation through attested tasks before they can transact at scale. Like a falcon that must hunt before it is trusted with the flock's meadow, an agent proves itself over time; a river of cheap fake identities cannot cross that cost barrier because each fake must separately pay the same work, stake, and time, making mass forgery unprofitable.
